A.note: Setup takes 8 players and builds a full 7-round, 28-game round-robin with court assignments and score inputs, and it has a standings tab, so the content is solid. Weaknesses: the green-and-white tables repeat with little variety, and the text is very small.

B.note: The 8-team bracket with example results and the court scoreboard (14:11, set and rally-point rules shown) sit side by side, which makes it the most polished and closest to real use. Weaknesses: the bracket text is small, and the screen hardly changed after the button presses.

C.note: Large text and a warm colour scheme make it readable, and it has both a bracket and a scoreboard. Weaknesses: the bracket is mostly '...' placeholders, the +1/+2/+5 scoreboard does not fit badminton rally scoring, and pop-up dialogs cover much of the screen.

D.note: The setup panel (format, target points) and the 8-team single-elimination bracket are neatly organised and look ready to print. Weaknesses: the text is small, the scoreboard screen never appears, and the screens after the button presses barely differ.
